audit.whatIsWrong: Four of seven rows disagreed with their own why text. whys[1] and whys[2] describe Aurora winning levels 2 and 3 while win[1] said Skill and win[2] said Yone; whys[3] and whys[4] both say 'even' while win[3] said Yone and win[4] said Aurora. The packet chart matches the whys exactly.
audit.why: The chart and the reasoning under it were rendering opposite answers.
audit.corrected: win[1]/phases[1].side = Aurora, win[2]/phases[2].side = Aurora, win[3]/phases[3].side = Skill, win[4]/phases[4].side = Skill. Level 1 (Aurora) and the last two rows (Yone) already agreed and were left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the entry treats her W as the only spike marker.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s and Between Worlds is 140/120/100s — the longest ultimate in the matchup. Twofold Hex is 9s at rank 1 from 900 range, which is why the first three levels are hers.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0], spikes[1], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabrications. (a) 'W blink through terrain / blink through walls' appears in spikes[0], early and wants.foe[1] — Riot's text says only that she leaps in a direction and enters the spirit realm on landing; there is no terrain traversal and no terrain flag on the ability. (b) The page tells you three times to 'pin her against her own R wall' — Between Worlds creates a slowing area that lets Aurora TELEPORT from one side to the other, so its edge is her escape, not a wall. (c) The one thing that actually decides the matchup is never mentioned: Across the Veil turns her INVISIBLE on landing, and Fate Sealed requires a target, so your 120-second ultimate cannot be cast on her while she is unseen.
audit.why: A player told to trap her against her ult's edge is being sent into the exact zone she teleports out of, and a player who ults into her W landing loses the ultimate for nothing.
audit.corrected: Terrain claim removed, the R described as a crossable zone, and the invisibility-blanks-Fate-Sealed interaction written into the cooldown block, the don'ts, mid and wants.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell and attack that damages you, and nothing on the page mentions anti-heal.
audit.why: Extended trades are exactly where that healing compounds, and extended trades are the plan the page recommends.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds added to breakdown.cooldowns and late.

edits.after: Full kit online, but her Q recast chunks you before you close. Hold the wave near your side and farm it out.

edits.before: Aurora pokes hard early with her Q (Twofold Hex) and can create distance with W (Across the Veil) blink through terrain. Her levels 1-3 poke chunks you before you engage; by 4-5 you can start closing with your Q dashes and it evens out.
edits.after: Aurora pokes hard early with Twofold Hex (Q, 900 range, 9s at rank 1), and Across the Veil (W, 22s) leaps her clear and turns her invisible on landing. Her levels 1-3 poke chunks you before you engage; by 4-5 your Q dashes start closing it.

edits.before: Aurora R (Between Worlds) zones a big area and can isolate you, but at 6 your all-in with Q3 knock-up into R matches her. If you can pin her against her own R wall, she can't W away and you win the trade.
edits.after: Between Worlds (R, 140s at rank 1) drops a slowing zone she can teleport across, so it is an escape as much as a threat — its edge is not a wall. Bait Across the Veil first; without it she cannot leave your combo.

edits.before: Aurora wins the early poke war: her Q (Twofold Hex) chunks you from range and her W (Across the Veil) lets her blink through walls to reset spacing whenever you try to close. Through levels 1-3 you're eating poke while she stays safe, so concede those trades and farm carefully. Don't burn tempo trying to catch her before you have the tools to.
edits.after: Aurora wins the early poke war: Twofold Hex chunks you from 900 range and the recast drags the curse back through you, while Across the Veil leaps her out and hides her whenever you try to close. Through levels 1-3 you're eating poke while she stays safe, so concede those trades and farm carefully. Don't burn tempo chasing her.

edits.before: By levels 4-5 it evens into a skill matchup — your Q dashes finally let you cross her poke range and force the trades her squishy frame doesn't want. The key is baiting her W blink; if she's used it, she has no escape from your combo. At 6 it stays roughly even: her R zones space, but if you pin her against her own wall with a Q3 knock-up into your R, she can't kite away.
edits.after: By levels 4-5 it evens into a skill matchup — your Q dashes finally cross her poke range and force the trades her squishy frame doesn't want. The key is baiting Across the Veil: it turns her invisible on landing, and Fate Sealed needs a target, so it will not fire while she is unseen. At 6 it stays even — Between Worlds slows a zone she can teleport across, so its edge will not trap her.

edits.before: After first item the lane tips to you. Aurora is a fragile mage whose only defensive tool is her W, so once you can eat her poke and still commit, your W shield and mixed DPS win the extended fight. With two-plus items you clearly out-scale — use E to follow her W and R displacements, stick to her, and close out fights her kit is built to avoid.
edits.after: After first item the lane tips to you. Aurora is fragile and her only outs are Across the Veil and her ultimate's teleport, so once you can eat the poke and still commit, Spirit Cleave's shield and mixed DPS win the extended fight. With two-plus items you clearly out-scale — bring Grievous Wounds for her passive healing and force the long fight.

notes: 'Pin her against her own R wall' appeared three times and is backwards — Between Worlds explicitly lets Aurora teleport from one side of the zone to the other. 'Blink through terrain/walls' for Across the Veil is also unsupported: Riot's text describes only a leap, and the ability carries no terrain flag. Per the aurora__yone mirror, I did not repeat the champion-wide 'W resets on takedown' claim; there is no takedown reset in Riot's text. The full layer still routes everything through focus.text 'Aurora Twofold Hex', which is fine — that IS her Q — but the full-layer prose calls it 'her escape' in several places (tldr, report[5], breakdown.spikes); her escape is Across the Veil. I fixed the cooldown block and dosFull[0].d; the rest would each need their own edit.
